paper.title: Predictability: Does the Flap of a Butterfly's Wings in Brazil Set Off a Tornado in Texas?
paper.zh_title: 可预测性：巴西蝴蝶扇动翅膀，会在得克萨斯引发龙卷风吗？
paper.author: Edward N. Lorenz
paper.description: 从蝴蝶效应的原始设问，理解微小差异如何限制长期天气预测。
paper.note: 本站双语导读，非原文全文或逐句翻译。此篇为 1972 年演讲，不是 1963 年《确定性的非周期流》论文；题目是研究问题，不是已经证明的单只蝴蝶因果故事。
paper.rights: 未确认原演讲的全文转载授权，本页仅提供本站编写的双语导读与来源链接。

blocks.en: The title presents a question about sensitivity: can extremely small differences between weather states grow into substantially different outcomes? A vivid image introduces a problem of prediction.
blocks.zh: 题目提出的是一个关于敏感性的问题：天气状态之间极小的差异，能否发展成明显不同的结果？一个生动的意象引出了预测问题。

blocks.en: Lorenz separates the evolution of a system from our ability to specify its starting state. Deterministic rules need not make long-range forecasts practically reliable.
blocks.zh: 洛伦兹把系统怎样演变，与我们能否准确确定它的初始状态区分开来。即使规则是确定的，长期预测也未必在实践中可靠。

blocks.en: Avoid reading the title as a demonstrated causal history of one butterfly and one tornado. The lecture asks how perturbations affect possibilities and the limits of forecasting.
blocks.zh: 不宜把题目读成已经证明的、某一只蝴蝶导致某一次龙卷风的故事。演讲讨论的是扰动怎样影响可能的结果，以及预测的限度。

blocks.en: Reading question: how much uncertainty in an initial measurement can a prediction tolerate? Think about this before equating a better model with an unlimited forecast horizon.
blocks.zh: 阅读时可以追问：一个预测能容忍多大的初始测量误差？在把更好的模型等同于无限长的预测期限之前，先想想这个问题。
